program_name: Economics and Finance with Data Science (Bachelor / Laurea Triennale)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). The programme is delivered entirely in English. apply.unito.it lists 'Study language: English' and the official overview states the programme 'is proposed as an internationally oriented course, offered entirely in English'. It is a single-university UNITO degree (not an interuniversity/joint degree) and it is a full standalone English-taught degree, not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy. Department of Economics, Social Studies, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ESOMAS - Dipartimento di Scienze economico-sociali e matematico-statistiche).
degree_class: UNITO internal degree-programme code: 2302L31 (course catalogue id 40375). The official Italian ministerial degree class (L-xx) could not be confirmed from an accessible official unito.it page; the programme microsite (efds.unito.it) and en.unito.it were unreachable during research. [uncertain]
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato / fixed quota of places) with a compulsory SAT admission test. apply.unito.it states: 'This is a course with a fixed quota of places, which requires candidates to pass an admission test (SAT) before enrolment.' Candidates must first sit the SAT (College Board) and then participate in one of the Apply@UniTo calls for admission; the calls themselves involve no further examination or test - selection is by ranking based on the SAT score. Note: one secondary UNITO-derived search snippet described the course as 'non-programmato' (open access), which contradicts the primary apply.unito.it text; the apply.unito.it portal (official application system) is treated as authoritative. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: 14 September 2026, 23:59:59 CET (a.y. 2026/27). application_deadline_non_eu: 15 April 2026 (a.y. 2026/27). entry_exam_or_test: SAT (College Board) - compulsory admission test taken before enrolment. Key points from official UNITO sources: (1) all candidates must sit the SAT and then apply in one of the Apply@UniTo calls; (2) the calls do not involve any further examination, test or interview; (3) SAT sittings are valid from 2 January 2025 up to the deadline stated in the admission call; (4) if the SAT is taken more than once, the score of the last sitting is used for the ranking; (5) the SAT may be taken before obtaining the secondary school leaving certificate. A candidate whose SAT Suite Math section score is below 400 points is admitted but must complete Additional Educational Obligations (OFA - remedial courses) in the first semester; no absolute minimum score is stated as a bar to admission in the later call. [uncertain - the SAT score/OFA threshold appears in UNITO SAT-degree material shared across UNITO's SAT-based English bachelors and could not be re-verified on the EFDS programme page itself]
academic_requirements: Entry qualification: high school / secondary education diploma. Official requirements from apply.unito.it: (a) the diploma must grant access to a university programme of the same level in the applicant's own country; (b) it must be obtained after at least 12 years of global education. If the diploma was obtained after fewer than 12 years of global schooling, it must be supplemented either with a declaration issued by the applicant's home university (with certified translation) attesting completion of all first-year university exams, or with a post-secondary qualification obtained at a non-university higher institution (with certified translation). If an academic proficiency exam is required in the applicant's country in order to access university education, the same exam is also required for admission to Italian universities. Quota: the programme has 50 available places reserved for non-European applicants residing abroad ('Territory requirements: This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad'). The total number of places (overall numero programmato) and any EU/Italian sub-quota are not published on the accessible official pages. Selection is by ranking on the SAT score; there is no GPA threshold, no motivation letter and no interview for this bachelor (motivation letters apply to UNITO postgraduate programmes only). Duration 3 years, 180 ECTS, full-time (full-time/part-time enrolment chosen yearly, with fees adjusted accordingly). [uncertain - total number of places]
language_requirements: English only; no Italian language requirement for this degree (it is fully English-taught, so the UNITO CLIQ B2 Italian certificate rule for Italian-taught open-access programmes does not apply). apply.unito.it lists the language requirement simply as 'English' with no named certificate or minimum score. The UNITO degree description states that applicants must have verbal comprehension in English at an advanced level, and that adequacy of initial preparation is verified through an evaluation test in English - in practice the compulsory SAT (which is administered in English) serves as that verification. No separate IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge/Duolingo score is listed as mandatory on any accessible official UNITO page for this programme. [uncertain - the programme's own 'Admission requirements' page on efds.unito.it, which is the page apply.unito.it links to for further detail, was unreachable and may list an additional English certificate option or exemption]
required_documents: Uploaded in the Apply@UniTo (apply.unito.it) online application: (1) valid passport or ID document (passport required for non-EU citizens); (2) high school diploma / final secondary school leaving certificate - original or certified copy, obtained after at least 12 years of schooling, with certified translation where required; (3) official transcript of records issued by the school with signature and seal - and, if the last two years were attended in a foreign education system, the transcript of school subjects for at least the last two years, with certified translation and legalisation if required; (4) SAT (College Board) score report; (5) where the diploma is based on fewer than 12 years of schooling, the supplementary university declaration or post-secondary qualification described under academic requirements; (6) payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call (the same amount whether one or two programmes are selected). Documents are accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish; documents in any other language must be accompanied by a certified/official translation into one of those four languages. After submission UNITO may request further documents (Declaration of Value, Statement of Verification, or a CIMEA statement of comparability), and the International Students Office may request additional documentation at the enrolment stage. Incomplete applications are not considered and cannot be resubmitted in the same academic year. Note: the motivation letter and English language certification listed by apply.unito.it apply to postgraduate programmes only, not to this bachelor.

uncertainty_notes: ACCESS PROBLEMS DURING RESEARCH (2026-09-01): (1) The programme's own microsite www.efds.unito.it and all other UNITO CampusNet microsites (esomas-en.unito.it, ecocomm-en.campusnet.unito.it, business-management.unito.it) were completely unreachable from every channel tried - direct fetch, sandboxed and unsandboxed curl over HTTPS and HTTP, and a rendering proxy - all returning connection refused / timeout against 130.186.3.24. The pages 'Key information', 'How to apply' and 'Admission requirements' on efds.unito.it therefore could NOT be read, even though apply.unito.it explicitly links to efds.unito.it/do/home.pl/View?doc=admission_requirements.html as the source of further admission detail. (2) en.unito.it, www.unito.it and unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it are behind Cloudflare/CAPTCHA bot protection and returned HTTP 403 / a human-verification page to every fetch attempt; content from those hosts is therefore reported only from search-engine snippets and is flagged accordingly. (3) The browser tools were unavailable in this session (Chrome extension not connected; browser navigation to efds.unito.it denied). CONSEQUENCE: apply.unito.it (which was fully accessible) is the primary verified source for this record. FIELD-LEVEL UNCERTAINTIES: (a) degree_class - the official Italian ministerial class (L-xx) is unverified; only UNITO's internal code 2302L31 (catalogue id 40375) is confirmed. One search summary mentioned 'Class L 18R' but this could not be confirmed on any accessible official page and may be a conflation with another programme, so it is NOT recorded as fact. (b) admission_type - apply.unito.it clearly describes a fixed quota of places with a compulsory SAT, while one UNITO-sourced search snippet described the course as 'non-programmato' (open access). This is an inconsistency between official UNITO surfaces; the apply.unito.it wording is used here. (c) Total number of places is not published on any accessible page - only the 50-place reservation for non-EU applicants residing abroad is confirmed. (d) SAT scoring rules (validity from 2 January 2025, last-sitting score used, OFA below 400 on the Math section) come from UNITO's general SAT/TOLC restricted-number bachelor page read via snippets, not from the EFDS programme page, and may be a UNITO-wide rule rather than an EFDS-specific one; the exact SAT registration cut-off date stated in the EFDS call was not obtainable. (e) English language requirements - apply.unito.it lists only 'English' with no certificate or score. A widely surfaced snippet giving concrete thresholds (TOEFL 50/59, TOEFL iBT 72/94, Duolingo >=100, IELTS 5.5, PTE >=46, Oxford Test of English >110, plus an age rule 'born between 2001 and 2008') actually originates from the University of Cassino (unicas.it) 'Economics with Data Science' programme, NOT from UNITO, and has been deliberately EXCLUDED from this record to avoid cross-university contamination. (f) application_deadline_non_eu - the 15 April 2026 date is the UNITO-wide second-call closing date for undergraduate programmes from apply.unito.it; the programme-specific call document confirming that EFDS non-EU-abroad applicants use exactly that window was not retrievable. The 14 September 2026 EU deadline is directly confirmed on the programme's own apply.unito.it page. (g) polito.it (Politecnico di Torino) was correctly excluded from this research as a separate institution.
